findings.title: skillFrontmatter.Name is never read
findings.body: No code reads `meta.Name`. The scan names skills only by folder or path, and this PR makes that explicit. The field and its yaml tag are dead, and could mislead a reader into thinking the frontmatter name matters. Remove it, or keep it with a comment saying why it is parsed.

findings.title: filepath.WalkDir does not follow a symlinked commands folder, so its commands silently disappear
findings.body: The old code used `os.ReadDir(root.dir)`, which follows a symlink at the root. `commandFiles` now calls `filepath.WalkDir(dir, ...)`. WalkDir `Lstat`s the root and does not follow symlinks. If `~/.claude/commands` or `<project>/.claude/commands` is a symlink to a directory (common when it points into a dotfiles repo), the callback gets the symlink as a non-directory entry whose name doesn't end in `.md`. It returns nil, so no commands are listed. The error is swallowed (`_ =`) and nothing is logged, so the `/` menu just omits every user command. Skill folders still work because they use `os.Stat`. Resolve the root first, e.g. `if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(dir); err == nil { dir = resolved }` before walking. Add a test with a symlinked commands dir. I did not run the code; this follows from the documented `WalkDir` behaviour.

findings.title: Is naming skills by folder right for Codex roots too?
findings.body: `scanSkillRoots` handles Claude and Codex roots with the same loop. The new comment and the test justify folder naming only by checking Claude Code 2.1. As I understand it, Codex's SKILL.md frontmatter requires a `name`, and Codex uses that name rather than the folder. If so, a Codex skill whose folder differs from its frontmatter name is listed under the wrong name. This predates the PR, but the PR now documents the rule as general. Can you confirm Codex behaves the same, or apply the rule per agent?
